description: C1–C2 practice sets for the grammar topics that had none, written by hand (2026-10-13); inversion from an earlier checked generation. Imported and published.

lessons.title: If I Had Taken That Job, I Would Be…: Mixed Conditionals
lessons.description: Practise conditionals that mix past and present time.

exercises.prompt: If I had studied medicine, I ___ a doctor now.
exercises.explanation: Past condition, present result: If + had + V3, would + base verb (now).

exercises.prompt: If she ___ so shy, she would have spoken to him at the party.
exercises.explanation: Present (general) condition, past result: If + past, would have + V3.

exercises.prompt: If we ___ (not / miss) the flight, we would be in Rome right now.
exercises.explanation: Past condition with a present result: hadn't missed … would be.

exercises.prompt: If I spoke French, I ___ (apply) for that job in Paris last year.
exercises.explanation: Present condition (I don't speak French), past result: would have applied.

exercises.prompt: “If I had saved money, I would have a car now” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Past cause (didn't save) → present result (no car now).

exercises.prompt: “If he would be more careful, he wouldn't have lost his wallet” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: No would in the if part: If he were more careful…
Past condition → present result: wouldn't be lost (now).

exercises.prompt: Match the halves.

pairs.If I hadn't stayed up so late,: I wouldn't be so tired now.
pairs.If she were more organised,: she wouldn't have missed the deadline.
pairs.If they had booked earlier,: they would be on holiday now.

exercises.explanation: Each sentence links a past or present cause to a result at the other time.

exercises.prompt: If I ___ afraid of heights, I would have gone skydiving with you.
exercises.explanation: A permanent fact (afraid of heights) uses the past: If I weren't afraid…

lessons.title: What I Need Is…: Cleft Sentences
lessons.description: Practise it-clefts and what-clefts to focus on the most important information.

exercises.prompt: ___ I need is a long holiday.
exercises.explanation: What-cleft: What + clause + is + focus.

exercises.prompt: It was my sister ___ broke the vase, not me!
exercises.explanation: It-cleft about a person: It was … who.

exercises.prompt: It ___ in 2019 that we first met.
exercises.explanation: It-cleft about a past time: It was … that.

exercises.prompt: What annoys me ___ people who talk during films.
exercises.explanation: What-cleft + is + focus.

exercises.prompt: “What I love about summer is the long evenings” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: What + clause + is + the focused part.

exercises.prompt: “It is the noise what bothers me” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: It-clefts use that or who: It is the noise that bothers me.
It was + focus + that + rest of the sentence.

exercises.prompt: Match the neutral sentence with its cleft version.

What I want is some peace.
It was Tom who called you.
It was on Friday that we left.

exercises.explanation: Cleft sentences move the important part into focus.

exercises.prompt: All I did ___ ask a simple question!
exercises.explanation: All + clause + was + focus: All I did was ask…

lessons.title: Never Have I Seen It: Inversion
lessons.description: You will practise using inversion after negative and limiting adverbials such as never, rarely, hardly and not only.

exercises.explanation: After Never at the start, the auxiliary verb comes before the subject: have I seen.
exercises.prompt: Never ___ such a funny video before.

exercises.explanation: The subject is my phone battery, a singular noun, and the verb last needs does.
exercises.prompt: Rarely ___ my phone battery last a whole day.

exercises.explanation: She is singular, so the auxiliary is has, and it comes before the subject.
exercises.prompt: Never ___ she been so nervous before an exam. (have/has)

exercises.explanation: After Never at the start we need inversion: Never have I felt.
exercises.prompt: “Never I have felt so happy” is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: Hardly is followed by had and the subject, then the past simple, for an event just before another.
exercises.prompt: Hardly ___ I got home when my friend called. (have/had)

exercises.explanation: Not only at the start needs inversion with did before he, and then the base verb.
exercises.prompt: Not only ___ the game late, but he also forgot his headphones.

exercises.explanation: Little at the start has a negative meaning, so did comes before she.
exercises.prompt: “Little did she know about the surprise party” is a correct sentence.

exercises.explanation: After Not until midnight, the auxiliary did comes before the subject he.
Each beginning uses inversion and needs the verb form that follows it.
exercises.prompt: Match the beginning with the correct ending.

exercises.explanation: No sooner is always followed by than.
exercises.prompt: No sooner had we left the café ___ it started to rain. (than/when)

exercises.explanation: Under no circumstances is a negative expression, so should comes before you.
exercises.prompt: Under no circumstances ___ your password with anyone online.

lessons.title: Feeling Tired, She Went Home: Participle Clauses
lessons.description: Practise -ing, -ed and having done clauses to make sentences shorter and more fluent.

exercises.prompt: ___ the door, she saw a huge spider.
exercises.explanation: Two actions at the same time with the same subject: -ing clause.

exercises.prompt: ___ in 1889, the Eiffel Tower is now a symbol of Paris.
exercises.explanation: Passive meaning (the tower was built): past participle.

exercises.prompt: ___ her homework, she went out with friends.
exercises.explanation: One action completed before the other: Having + past participle.

exercises.prompt: ___ (not / know) what to say, he stayed silent.
exercises.explanation: Negative -ing clause: Not + -ing, giving the reason.

exercises.prompt: “Walking home, the rain started” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: The subject must be the same: the rain wasn't walking. Correct: Walking home, I got caught in the rain.

exercises.prompt: “Shocked by the news, he called his mum” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Past participle clause with the same subject (he was shocked).
Having + V3 shows the earlier action and the reason.

exercises.prompt: Match the full sentence with the participle clause.

Feeling tired, I went to bed.
pairs.The film, which was directed by her, won: Directed by her, the film won a prize.
pairs.After she had read the email, she replie: Having read the email, she replied.

exercises.explanation: -ing = active/same time; -ed = passive; having done = earlier action.

exercises.prompt: The girl ___ next to Sam is my cousin.
exercises.explanation: Reduced relative clause: the girl (who is) sitting.

lessons.title: I Suggest That He Be…: The Subjunctive
lessons.description: Practise the subjunctive after suggest, insist, demand and in fixed expressions.

exercises.prompt: The doctor recommended that he ___ more water.
exercises.explanation: After recommend that: subjunctive = base form for every subject.

exercises.prompt: It is essential that every student ___ on time.
exercises.explanation: It is essential that + subjunctive: be.

exercises.prompt: She insisted that he ___ (leave) immediately.
exercises.explanation: insist that + base form, even with he.

exercises.prompt: We demand that the company ___ (not / raise) prices again.
exercises.explanation: Negative subjunctive: not + base form (no do).

exercises.prompt: “I suggest that she applies for the scholarship” is formal subjunctive.
exercises.explanation: The subjunctive form is apply (no -s): I suggest that she apply.

exercises.prompt: “If I were you, I'd say yes” uses a subjunctive form.
exercises.explanation: were with I is a past subjunctive.
It is vital that + subject + be + past participle (passive subjunctive).

exercises.prompt: Match the fixed expression with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: These old fixed phrases keep the subjunctive form.

exercises.prompt: The teacher asked that we ___ our phones off.
exercises.explanation: ask that + base form: we turn.

lessons.title: It Would Seem That…: Hedging and Softening
lessons.description: Practise ways to sound careful and polite: it seems, tend to, might, somewhat.

exercises.prompt: ___ that the results are not as good as we expected.
exercises.explanation: It would seem that… is a careful, polite way to state a conclusion.

exercises.prompt: Teenagers ___ to spend more time online than adults.
exercises.explanation: tend to + verb makes a general claim less absolute.

exercises.prompt: Your essay is ___ too long. Could you cut a few paragraphs? (somewhat / extremely)
exercises.explanation: somewhat softens criticism; extremely makes it stronger.

exercises.prompt: There ___ to be a problem with your booking. (seems / is)
exercises.explanation: There seems to be… is softer than There is…

exercises.prompt: “This may suggest that the theory is wrong” sounds more cautious than “This proves the theory is wrong”.
exercises.explanation: may suggest is a hedge; proves is a strong claim.

exercises.prompt: “Arguably” makes a claim sound more certain.
exercises.explanation: arguably means it can be argued — it softens the claim.
It could be argued that… presents an opinion cautiously.

exercises.prompt: Match the direct sentence with the softened one.

I'm not sure that's quite right.
The plan might run into difficulties.

exercises.explanation: Hedging uses negatives of positive words, modals and softer verbs.

exercises.prompt: The data appear to ___ a link between sleep and memory.
exercises.explanation: appear to + base verb: a careful academic hedge.
